subject: Scope & Owners: Multilingual POC — model tiering, acceptance gates, next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@linguaai.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + proposed POC scope and owners

Hi Lina — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick written recap so we have a single source of truth and can move to a kick-off.

Summary of what we heard
- Goal: pilot an LLM-based assistant to handle multilingual customer support routing and short answer resolution for English, Spanish, French, German. Target is to reduce human first-response time and deflection of tier-1 tickets.
- Volume: ~12k monthly conversations across channels (chat + email); initial POC traffic will be a 5% shadow + 5% live sample per language.

Proposed POC scope (6 weeks)
1) Data & infra prep (week 0–1): sample export (10k rows), redaction guidance, sandbox creds.
2) Model selection & baseline (week 2): run evaluation harness across candidate models for each language.
3) Integration & routing (week 3–4): connect Redwood API, set up fallback routing and KV caching.
4) Acceptance & handover (week 5–6): run acceptance tests, establish monitoring, run a 48h live validation window.

Model tiering suggestion (initial):
- Primary (English heavy): Llama-2-13B-q4f (optimized) for developer/throughput balance
- Multilingual coverage: Mistral-Instruct-7B for spanish/french/german tests
- Fast/fallback: vicuna-13b-v1.5-quant as a low-cost fallback route for degraded capacity

Success criteria (high level)
- Intent classification accuracy >= 92% (en), >=88% (es/fr/de) on blinded eval set
- NLU extraction F1 >= 0.90 for required entities
- Latency p95 < 800ms for live path
- Hallucination/incorrect answer rate < 2% on curated red-team prompts

Owners & next steps
- Aditya Rao (sales): commercial lead, SOW & kickoff scheduling
- Monica Patel (CS): POC project lead, acceptance checklist, evaluation harness
- Vivek Kulkarni (SE): model configuration, infra setup, quantization guidance

Immediate asks
- Lina: confirm scope and the four languages + whether you want post-message translation (Redwood can provide in-pipeline translation but it changes latency/cost).
- Procurement: indicate contact and PO timing if SOW needed before kick-off.

I attached a short model-matrix and will share a success-metrics sheet shortly. If this looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for a 30-min kickoff next Tue/Wed.

— Aditya
Aditya Rao | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Lina Gomez <lina@linguaai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@linguaai.com
Date: 2028-03-22T11:04:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed POC scope and owners

Thanks Aditya — that aligns with what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:
- Confirming languages: EN / ES / FR / DE — correct. We do not need translation in-path for this pilot (we'd prefer native-language models where possible to reduce noise).
- Data & privacy: we can provide a redacted export within 3 business days. We will need Redwood's SOC2 report and a data retention/offboarding statement before we push any production-like data.
- Commercial: procurement looped in — we prefer a 6-week fixed-scope SOW. Budget is constrained; can you share a rough estimate for the POC cost (GPU hrs + integration support) so procurement can triage?

I'll also confirm who will be the technical contact on our side (likely Sara in engineering). Please include an NDA/SOW draft in the follow-up.

— Lina
Lina Gomez | Head of Product, LinguaAI
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Cc: Lina Gomez <lina@linguaai.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T15:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + proposed POC scope and owners — infra & model notes

Adding technical notes from our side so Monica and LinguaAI have concrete items for the evaluation plan: 

1) Candidate models & config notes- Llama-2-13B (q4f) — good throughput, best for eng-heavy prompts; recommend 8k context for chat history retention.- Mistral-Instruct-7B — strong multi-language instruction following; use for ES/FR/DE validation.- Vicuna-13B-quant — fallback route when primary is at capacity; lower cost but expect slightly higher hallucination rates.

2) Quantization & latency- Recommend q4f or q8_0 where available to hit p95 < 800ms for 1–2k token responses on an A100-class node.- We'll provide a recommended instance mix and estimated GPU-hours once we see expected concurrency (you mentioned 5% live sample — please confirm EPS).

3) Routing & fallbacks- Strategy: language-detect -> route to language-optimized model -> if latency threshold breached or error then route to fallback with degraded response policy.- Use a small prefix cache (KV) for recent threads to cut cost and latency on follow-ups.

4) Evaluation harness & metrics (Monica please own test harness)- Automated eval: per-language holdout sets (1k examples each) measuring intent accuracy, entity F1, and semantic similarity (embedding-based) vs human labels.- Live validation: 48h live window measuring p95 latency, error rate, and user-reported correctness.

5) Data handling- We will support redaction helpers; recommend LinguaAI remove PII before upload. Redwood will keep sandbox logs 30 days for POC unless you request shorter retention. Provide SOC2 report as requested.

I can produce a model-matrix PDF with expected latency/cost per 1k tokens by tomorrow.

— Vivek
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Lina Gomez <lina@linguaai.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T09:18:00Z
Subject: POC success metrics & checklist (draft attached)

Hi team — attaching the draft POC-success-metrics.xlsx and a short model-matrix PDF. Highlights from the checklist (please review and flag changes):

Acceptance tests (automated + manual)- Intent accuracy thresholds: EN >=92%, ES/FR/DE >=88% on blinded eval set.- Extraction F1 >=0.90 on entities used for routing (ticket_type, product_id, priority).- Hallucination audit: sampled 200 red-team prompts, <=2% incorrect assertions.- Latency: p95 < 800ms for the primary live path; fallback p95 target <1.2s.

Operational SLOs and rollback- Error budget: 1% total error rate during live validation window; if crossed, automatic rollback to baseline rule-based routing.

Ownership matrix- Monica Patel: POC project owner, acceptance gate sign-off, post-POC handover doc- Vivek Kulkarni: infra & model config, profiling & quantization recommendations- Aditya Rao: commercial approvals, SOW finalization, calendar coordination- LinguaAI technical contact: provides redacted data, validates language holdouts

Timeline (target)
- Thu week 0: receive redacted export + SOC2 link- Mon week 1: infrastructure provisioned, baseline evaluations started- Week 2–3: integration and routing + internal acceptance tests- Week 4: 48h live validation window- Week 5: final acceptance and handover

Next immediate items
- LinguaAI: confirm redaction timeline and technical contact.
- Aditya: please share SOW draft & ballpark cost estimate.

Attachments:
- POC-success-metrics.xlsx (spreadsheet)- model-matrix.pdf (summary of latency & cost by model)

Thanks — I’ll update the sheet with threshold examples and a simple evaluation checklist for the holdout harness.

— Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
